# Method notes from issue 4527

Observations about the *method* and the tooling, not about the issue. Nothing here belongs in
`comment.md`.

## 1. A runtime-only symptom needs decomposing before `cmd.txt`, not after

The report's symptom is a D3D12 `CreatePipelineState` rejection — no compiler observes it. The
useful move was writing `expected.md` as a decomposition ("the compile is clean" AND "the
container is invalid or unsigned") with a **pre-registered mapping to a status**: not-A ⇒
`changed-behavior`. Measurement then hit not-A immediately, and the classification was already
decided by a document written before any evidence existed. Without that, "it errors instead" is
easy to record as `does-not-repro`, which would have closed a live bug.

## 2. The signing instrument needed a control more than the diagnostic did

"The container is unsigned" is an absence-shaped predicate and matches the whole world whenever
`dxil.dll` is missing or `-Vd` is passed. Both the failing shader *and* a known-good one come back
with an all-zero digest under `-Vd`. The control is what makes the measurement mean anything, and
it belongs in the same capture file, above the result — `manual-case-unsigned-container.txt`
therefore opens with "READ THE CONTROL BEFORE THE RESULT". Generalizable: any capture whose
headline is an absence should be laid out control-first.

## 3. `--version` is not universally available, and a capture must say so

`dxc --version` fails on v1.4.1907 with `Unknown argument: '--version'`. A generator that prints
`[version]` per release will happily record that failure string as if it were a version. Left as
recorded, with a header line explaining that pre-v1.8 binaries are identified by tag and build
date instead. Deleting the line would have been the wrong fix; the failure *is* the datapoint.

## 4. v1.4.1907's validator prints raw pointer addresses, so its output is not reproducible

`at 0x1ca56295df0 inside block #0 of function mainPS Instructions must be of an allowed type` —
the address differs on every run. Re-running `measure.py` therefore produces a capture that is not
byte-identical to the previous one even though every verdict is unchanged (measured: 6 differing
lines, all of them addresses in the v1.4.1907 block). Worth knowing before treating a diff of a
regenerated capture as a change in behaviour, and worth avoiding in a predicate regex.

## 5. A synthetic command line in a capture — the #2922 trap, met live

`measure.py` copies two DLLs with `shutil.copy2` to build a "no `dxil.dll`" layout. My first
version printed that as `$ copy <src> <dst>`, which is a command line that never ran. Fixed by
printing `[setup] shutil.copy2 of … into …` — a different prefix from `$ `, so a reader can see at
a glance which lines are executed commands and which are described actions. The rule generalizes:
`$ ` should be reserved for `subprocess.list2cmdline(argv)` output and nothing else.

## 6. Control files generated by byte replacement must preserve length

Generating `control-member-const.hlsl` from the attachment by replacing the `TEST_CASE` define
asserted on equal file length and failed, because the replacement token was shorter. Padding it to
the same length keeps every line and column number identical to the repro's, which is what lets
diagnostics from the two files be compared directly. The assertion was worth having.

## 7. The `godbolt` banner must not contain the string a reader is told to look for

CE compiles with `-Zi -Qembed_debug`, so the banner text ends up inside the shader's embedded
source. A banner that quotes the exact error string would make that string appear in the *passing*
control pane's output too, via the embedded source, and a reader searching for it would find it
everywhere. Wrote the banner structurally instead ("the failure is not a syntax error — it is DXIL
validation that rejects the result, naming the array's mangled symbol"). No literal diagnostic
text.

## 8. `--source` earns its keep when a comparison compiler cannot run the original

Clang's HLSL backend cannot lower `SV_Target`, so a pixel-shader pane would have filled with stage
errors that say nothing about the issue. `godbolt --source repro-cs.hlsl` published a compute
restatement instead. Two things made that safe, and both should be standard when translating a
repro for CE: **(a)** the restatement was run locally first, under the same predicate, and scored
`repro` before being published; **(b)** the translation carries its own control in the same file
behind `-D CONTROL_NO_STATIC`, so one pane differs from another by a single token. A translated
repro without a local pre-check is an assertion, not a measurement.

## 9. `-dumpbin` of the emitted container answers linkage questions that stdout cannot

The validator's phrase "External declaration … is unused" reads like a missing definition. It is
not — it is the validator's word for non-internal linkage. Disassembling the container and
printing every module-scope global (`manual-case-container-symbol.txt`) settled it in two lines,
and the control turned it from an observation into a mechanism: the working shader's array arrives
as `internal constant [9 x float]` (lowered), the failing one as
`linkonce_odr constant [3 x <3 x float>]` (not lowered). Reading a diagnostic's wording as a claim
about the IR is a trap; disassemble and look.

## 10. `audit --issue <n>` gave no false comfort, but it is a completeness check only

`audit --issue 4527` reported "no missing evidence" while `notes.md`, `comment.md` and the verdict
were all still unwritten. It checks that the evidence a recorded verdict refers to exists — useful,
parallel-safe, and not a substitute for the step-by-step checklist. Worth stating in a brief so a
worker does not read a clean `audit` as "done".
